# Apocalypse of Peter — Chapter 1
**Agent:** SOPHIA (Consensus)
**Source:** Akhmim Fragment / Ethiopic MS, Apocalypse of Peter 1

---

## Consensus Translation

1. As he sat upon the Mount of Olives, his disciples came to him one by one and implored him, saying: "Make known to us the signs of your coming and of the end of the age."

2. Our Lord answered and said to us: "Take heed that no one leads you astray. Many will come in my name saying, 'I am the Christ.' Do not believe them, and do not draw near to them.

3. For deceivers and false prophets will arise and establish various teachings and doctrines, ensnaring those who are perishing.

4. These will be sons of perdition. Then God my Father will come, to raise the dead and to judge the living and the dead and to reward every person according to their works."

5. He showed us in his right hand the souls of all humanity, and in the palm of his right hand the image of what will be accomplished in the last day.

6. And I saw how the wicked were delivered to the angels of punishment, who drove them toward a place of outer darkness.

7. He said to us: "When the fig tree puts forth its shoots, in the last days deceivers and false prophets will arise and teach various doctrines, ensnaring those who are perishing.

8. The parable of the fig tree is to be understood thus: when its shoots spring up and its branches grow, the end of the world will come."

9. I, Peter, answered and said to him: "Explain to me also the parable of the fig tree. How shall we understand it?"

10. The Lord answered me and said: "Do you not understand that the fig tree is the house of Israel? A man planted a fig tree in his garden; it bore no fruit, and he sought fruit on it for many years. When he found none, he said to the keeper of his garden: 'Uproot this fig tree, that it may not render our ground barren.'

11. The keeper of the garden said to him: 'Allow us to tend it once more — to dig around it and water it; and if it bears no fruit, we will straightway remove its roots from the garden and plant another in its place.'

12. Have you not understood that the fig tree is the house of Israel? Truly I say to you: when its branches have sprouted in the last days, false Christs will come, stirring up hope and saying, 'I am the Christ, who has now come into the world.'

13. And when they perceive the wickedness of the deeds of these false Christs, many will follow them and deny the one whom our fathers praised — the first Christ, whom they crucified, thereby sinning greatly.

14. But this deceiver is not the Christ. When they reject him, he will kill with the sword, and there will be many martyrs."

15. Then the branches of the fig tree — the house of Israel — will shoot forth; and many will be martyred at his hand.

16. "Enoch and Elijah will be sent to teach them that this is the Deceiver who must come into the world to perform signs and wonders and to deceive.

17. Therefore those who die at his hand will be martyrs, counted among the good and righteous martyrs who have pleased God in their lives."

---

## Textual Notes

- **"Sons of perdition" (v.4):** All agents retained; the phrase is a fixed early Christian idiom (cf. John 17:12, 2 Thess 2:3).
- **"Sons / children of perdition" (v.4):** PNEUMA loosened to "children of destruction"; consensus prefers the traditional form.
- **"Outer darkness" (v.6):** Retained from Matthew's eschatological discourse; likely a deliberate echo.
- **"House of Israel" for fig tree (vv. 10–12):** All agents agreed on transparency of the allegory; SOPHIA retains the interpretive equation while letting the parable stand.
- **"Enoch and Elijah" (v.16):** The two eschatological witnesses of Rev 11 and intertestamental tradition; not glossed.

---
*SOPHIA synthesizes EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA, preferring formal clarity and received theological vocabulary while adopting PNEUMA's readability where it does not sacrifice precision.*
